subject: Clarification: Tiered Commit, Burst Credits, and Overages (RFI ID: MED-2026-51)
messages:
From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@medisine.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medisine.com>

Subject: RFI MED-2026-51 — commercial clarifications

Hannah,

Thanks for the quick turn on the RFI intake. We received the commercial appendix but need a couple of clarifications before we circulate to our finance and legal teams. Specifically: 

1) Token pricing granularity — can you confirm the per-1k token list price for each model family included in the appendix (e.g., base LLM, generation-optimized, embeddings)? The spreadsheet lists blended bands but our CFO requires explicit per-1k lines for forecasting.

2) Commit tiers & acceleration credits — how do you apply acceleration credits when a customer front-loads committed consumption (e.g., pays for Q1–Q2 up front)? Do committed credits convert to burst credits, or do they lower the invoice rate immediately?

3) Burst credits and caps — the RFI mentions burst credits that replenish monthly. Is there a hard cap on burst consumption as a percentage of committed capacity per billing period? Also, how are bursts invoiced if they exceed the cap?

4) True-up cadence and invoice mechanics — do you support quarterly true-ups with monthly interim metering? If quarterly, how are overage discounts applied retroactively on the invoice?

I attached our commercial worksheet (MED-RFP-Commercial.xlsx) with highlighted rows. If you can provide concise answers and an updated commercial sheet with explicit per-1k rows, that would help accelerate legal review.

Best,
Alan
Alan Cho

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Alan — thanks for the detail. Answers inline and attached an updated commercial appendix. Summary:

• Per-1k token list prices: Provided as explicit lines in the attached "Redwood-RFI-MED-2026-51-commercial.xlsx" for each model family (base, generation, instruction-tuned, embeddings). We also include an "effective blended rate" row for multi-model bundles.

• Commit acceleration credits: When customers pre-pay (or accelerate) committed capacity, the pre-paid units are applied first to consumption and reduce effective per-token invoiced rates immediately; we do not convert pre-paid units into separate "burst" tokens. Instead we implement an acceleration credit ladder (see sheet) that provides larger marginal discounts for front-loaded purchase volumes.

• Burst credits & caps: Customers receive a monthly burst allowance (as % of committed capacity) to absorb unexpected spikes. The default cap is 40% of committed monthly capacity; customers can opt for higher caps with a small surcharge. Usage beyond the burst cap is billed at overage list rates unless a negotiated overage ladder applies.

• True-ups & invoicing: We support monthly metering with quarterly true-ups by default. During a quarterly true-up we apply any committed discounts retroactively to the invoice period and issue credit/debit adjustments on the true-up invoice. We can support annual true-ups on request.

Attachments: updated commercial appendix (with per-1k rows), term sheet PDF.

--- draft end ---

My notes: keep the burst cap default numeric (40%) — makes it easier for finance — and include optional accelerated-credit ladder (0–3 tiers). Marissa: can you run the updated numbers for the 3-tier acceleration ladder we discussed (standard, gold, platinum) and paste them into the spreadsheet?

Alan — thanks again for the good questions. Please find concise answers below and an updated commercial appendix attached. I’ve kept the structure CFO-friendly (explicit per-1k lines, then blended rows).

Key responses (high level):

1) Per-1k token pricing (list) — explicit rows included in the attached spreadsheet (tab: PRICING). Line items: 
  - Base family (small/medium): $0.80 / 1K tokens
  - Generation-optimized (large gen): $2.10 / 1K tokens
  - Instruction-tuned (safety/chain): $3.40 / 1K tokens
  - Embeddings: $1.00 / 1K tokens
  - Multi-model bundle: shows blended effective rates based on weighted usage; CFO can use the explicit rows to map to their usage mix.

2) Commit acceleration credits — mechanism: when a customer prepays for future committed units, those units are applied to consumption immediately and reduce the effective invoice rate in the month they are applied. We do not morph pre-paid units into a separate pool of "burst tokens." Instead we apply an acceleration discount ladder (tab: ACCELERATION) — higher front-loaded purchases get larger marginal discounts. Example: upfront purchase equal to 6 months of commit -> additional 4% off list for the accelerated portion.

3) Burst credits and caps — default burst allowance: 40% of committed monthly capacity. Optional higher caps (60%/100%) are available for an incremental surcharge (see tab: BURST_POLICIES). If burst consumption exceeds the chosen cap in a billing period, the excess is billed at overage list rates. We also support a negotiated overage tier for high-velocity enterprise customers.

4) True-up cadence and invoice mechanics — default model: monthly metering + quarterly true-up. During the quarterly true-up we: (a) reconcile committed vs actual consumption; (b) apply the committed discount ladder retroactively to covered consumption; (c) issue a single true-up adjustment invoice (credit or debit). For customers requesting quarterly invoicing only, we can move to quarterly metering with the same reconciliation cadence.

Attachments included:
- Redwood-RFI-MED-2026-51-commercial.xlsx (pricing tabs: PRICING, ACCELERATION, BURST_POLICIES)
- redwood-term-sheet.pdf (high-level commercial terms, invoicing cadence, termination & refund mechanics)

If you’d like, we can run a quick sensitivity showing effective blended rates for Medisine’s three usage profiles (conservative, expected, high) — I can include that in a follow-up.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-RFI-MED-2026-51-commercial.xlsx (spreadsheet); redwood-term-sheet.pdf (PDF)
